questions.prompt: Replace the direct object: « Je regarde le film. »
questions.explanation: Le is the masculine singular direct-object pronoun before regarde.

questions.prompt: Replace « Marie »: « Tu connais Marie ? »
questions.explanation: Connaître takes a direct object: la replaces Marie.

questions.prompt: Replace the indirect object: « Je téléphone à Paul. »
questions.explanation: Téléphoner à takes an indirect object pronoun: lui.

questions.prompt: Complete: « Nous écrivons à nos parents. Nous ___ écrivons. »
questions.explanation: Leur replaces an indirect plural recipient, à nos parents.

questions.prompt: Complete the negative: « Je ___ vois pas. » referring to two people.
questions.explanation: Ne precedes the object pronoun and the verb: je ne les vois pas.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct pronoun placement in a compound tense.
questions.explanation: The object pronoun precedes the auxiliary in passé composé.

questions.prompt: Choose the past participle agreement: « Les lettres ? Je les ai ___. »
questions.explanation: With avoir, the past participle agrees with a preceding direct object: les lettres.

questions.prompt: Which replacement means 'I speak to her'?
questions.explanation: Parler à quelqu'un requires an indirect object pronoun, lui.

questions.prompt: Replace « à Paris » with an adverbial pronoun: « Nous allons à Paris. »
questions.explanation: Y replaces a destination introduced by à.

questions.prompt: Read: « Léa lui envoie une carte. » Who is the recipient?
questions.explanation: Lui represents the indirect recipient of the card.

questions.prompt: Read: « Ils les ont retrouvées. » What can the -ées ending indicate here?
choices: A preceding feminine plural direct object.
questions.explanation: Retrouvées agrees with a preceding feminine plural direct object les.

questions.prompt: Read: « Elle ne lui a pas répondu. » What did not happen?
choices: She did not visit a place.
She did not reply to that person.
She did not see a film.
questions.explanation: Répondre à takes lui, and the negative surrounds the auxiliary.

questions.prompt: Read: « J'y suis allé samedi. » What can y refer to?
questions.explanation: Y often refers to a place introduced by à or another location phrase.

questions.prompt: Read: « Elle en parle souvent. » What can en replace?
questions.explanation: En can replace de plus a topic in parler de.

questions.prompt: Read: « Nous la connaissions depuis longtemps. » What is la here?
choices: A definite article before a noun.
questions.explanation: La stands alone before connaissions as a direct-object pronoun.

questions.prompt: Read: « Les photos, je les ai prises hier. » What explains prises?
choices: Agreement with the preceding feminine plural object.
Agreement with hier as an adverb.
questions.explanation: Les refers to photos, preceding avoir and requiring feminine plural agreement.

questions.prompt: Read: « Nous leur avons donné les clés. » Who received the keys?
questions.explanation: Leur marks the indirect recipients of the keys.

questions.prompt: Read: « Je ne l'ai pas reconnue. » What can the -e in reconnue indicate?
choices: A feminine singular direct object placed before avoir.
questions.explanation: The past participle agrees with a preceding feminine singular direct object.

questions.prompt: A friend asks « Tu connais cette chanson ? » Choose a reply using a pronoun.
questions.explanation: Chanson is feminine singular and the direct object becomes la.

questions.prompt: You call two friends. Replace « à mes amis » in « Je parle à mes amis ».
questions.explanation: À mes amis is plural indirect recipient; leur replaces it.

questions.prompt: Correct: « J'ai les vus hier ».
questions.explanation: Les must precede the auxiliary ai for a direct object.

questions.prompt: You visited the museum yesterday and want to avoid repeating its name.
questions.explanation: Y can replace the previously mentioned museum as a destination.

questions.prompt: You discuss a project often. Replace « de ce projet » in « Nous parlons de ce projet ».
questions.explanation: En replaces a de-phrase in parler de.

questions.prompt: A student writes « Je ne vois les pas ». Which correction works?
questions.explanation: The object pronoun follows ne and precedes the conjugated verb.

questions.prompt: Replace a previously mentioned girl in « J'ai rencontré cette fille ».
questions.explanation: The feminine direct object l' is before avoir, requiring rencontrée.

questions.prompt: You thank your teacher by speaking to her: choose the correct object.
questions.explanation: Dire merci à quelqu'un takes the indirect pronoun lui.

questions.prompt: Two girls were seen yesterday. Which sentence uses correct agreement?
questions.explanation: Les replaces a feminine plural direct object before avoir, so vues agrees.
